title: Shard-aware trace hook and fidelity guardrail for edge SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Edge SDKs and lightweight proxies drop or mutate high-cardinality propagation headers when a request is sharded across networks or queued. This causes trace fragmentation and incorrect latency attribution in the console. Goal: implement a shard-aware trace hook that stabilizes a minimal provenance envelope (lightweight deterministic IDs + sampling hints) and a fidelity guardrail in SDK middleware that rejects or repairs malformed propagation at the SDK boundary. The hook should be low-overhead, opt-in per SDK version, and compatible with existing OpenTelemetry and our envelope format. Deliver a small runtime shim plus an SDK middleware pattern and tests for HTTP/gRPC/websocket clients.
acceptance_criteria: SDK hook added to Node and Python SDKs behind feature flag; default off for older SDK versions
End-to-end trace continuity for 99.9% of synthetic inter-region sharded requests in canary test cluster
Console shows correct parent/child relationships and single request latency for sharded flows in the latency dashboard tests
Unit and integration tests for malformed header repair logic with >=95% deterministic recovery
A concise migration doc and demo script added to /docs/confluence (link provided)
notes: Design constraints: Keep envelope < 512 bytes. Use deterministic shard-seed + short provenance stamp to avoid PII.
Prior art: see ENG-21478 for correlation header translator and ENG-30321 for instrumentation guidelines.
Trade-offs: aggressive repair may hide upstream buggy proxies; guardrail will emit a telemetry metric for repaired headers to detect bad intermediaries.
Performance target: additional CPU < 0.3% p50 for common request path; memory overhead per request < 120 bytes.
Compatibility: must interoperate with OTEL W3C traceparent and baggage; fall back to legacy X-Redwood-Trace when present.
decisions: Use a compact binary-safe base64 envelope with version byte and 24-bit deterministic shard-seed rather than full UUID to reduce header size.
Implement repair logic that prefers OTEL traceparent when valid, else constructs parent using shard-seed + timestamp window for continuity.
Expose a 'fidelity_hint' tag in spans for repaired headers so dashboards can filter repaired vs native traces.
Feature gated rollout: Node v2.4+ and Python v1.9+ behind 'shard_propagation' flag; server side runtime will accept both new envelope and legacy headers.
testing_plan: Synthetic canary: 10k sharded requests/sec across 3 regions with induced header trimming by proxies; verify trace stitch rate and latency stability
Unit tests: header encode/decode edge cases, non-UTF8 payloads, and maliciously long headers
Integration tests: Node and Python SDKs with HTTP/gRPC clients and server runtime that accepts both envelopes
Metric assertions: a new metric observability.shard_repair.count emitted when repair occurs; alert threshold > 0.1% of requests in prod
implementation_notes: Runtime change: accept new envelope format and map to internal context with provenance fields for console display
SDK change: middleware hook order must run before existing sampling and before user middleware that might inspect headers
Backwards compatibility: servers will continue to accept legacy X-Redwood-Trace and OTEL headers; if both present, prefer explicit OTEL traceparent
Telemetry: add debug log level that can emit original raw header, runtime-decoded envelope, and repair decision for debugging in canary
